newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says low 1996 rates set stage for 1997 growth.
newsitem.headline: Bonn says low 1996 rates set stage for 1997 growth.

text.p: The German economy was lifted out of the doldrums at the end of 1996 while low interest rates that year are a key factor that could spur growth in 1997, the economics ministry said on Wednesday.
But despite renewed expansion of the economy, there was little benefit to the job market.

"In contrast to the unsatisfactory situation on the labour market there was a series of positive factors at the end of the year the set the conditions for further economic development" the ministry said in its monthly economic report.
"In addition to low interest rates and the favourable mark exchange rates, these include undoubtedly price stability which has virtually been achieved," it added.
